Reading this thread strikes a chord with me. On the day of my graduation ceremony, I opened my diploma cover to find a note stating that I needed to pay my bill to get my diploma.
Reading this thread strikes a chord with me. On the day of my graduation ceremony, I opened my diploma cover to find a note stating that I needed to pay my bill to get my diploma.

I worked my way through nursing school, despite multiple professors telling me it wasn’t possible. I graduated with honors and 2 minors, from a private liberal arts university with a well-respected school of nursing.

My parents, younger siblings, and both grandmothers (my only living grandparents) drove 500+ miles to attend my graduation. They were so proud of me and I was excited to share that special day with them.

I grew up below the poverty line. I’m the only child from my family to graduate from college and I’m the first person on my dad’s side of the family to pursue higher education. My parents could only occasionally afford to help me pay for my books.

Today my diploma & nsg license are framed and displayed on my wall. I’m proud of what I’ve accomplished. I’m grateful to my family for all of their support. But there will always be a part of me that will remember how it felt the moment I realized I still didn’t have my diploma.
